minutes.headline: Select Board reprogrammed ARPA funds and allocated about $353,000 to requests using median rankings; vice chair recall pressure aired.
minutes.summary: The board heard extensive public comment about the vice chair and a possible recall, then took up ARPA funds. It voted to redirect two ARPA lines, chose the median over the average for ranking requests, and voted to commit the final allocation list. Other business: St. Bonifice Oktoberfest license, interim town manager report, Chapter 70 letter from the school committee, flat hill speed limit discussion, and a request for an HR state-of-the-organization report.

public_comment.topic: Resident urged the vice chair to resign, citing rule violations and the effect on recruiting a town manager; said she would support a recall otherwise.
School committee member speaking for himself asked the board to reconsider the $10,000 request to finish the track and field drainage assessment, saying the turf field is at end of life.
Library trustees chair praised the vice chair as board liaison to the library and lamented strife on the board.
Resident urged civility, lamented vacancies and board dysfunction, and thanked the interim town manager for attention to the Council on Aging.
Resident defended the vice chair, said there is no groundswell for removal, and urged people not to sign the recall petition.
Resident said he is researching a charter review committee under Chapter 43B and a petition requiring 15% of registered voters.
Council on Aging director disagreed with the earlier comparison of the interim manager to the former manager and said the former manager supported the COA.

votes.motion: Approve special event license and one-day wine and beer license for St. Bonifice parish Oktoberfest on September 21, 2024, rain date September 22.
Redirect ARPA consultant line to ARPA Administration and IT staffing challenges, and FY23 tax assessment support line to FY24/FY25 valuation services.
Approve minutes of the August 6, 2024 meeting.
Commit the ARPA funds as stated by the chair in the final updated median allocation.

budget_items.what_was_said: The school committee asked that the added Chapter 70 over the governor's proposal be appropriated to the school department at the November special town meeting; the board agreed to forward it to the interim town manager for inclusion.
A resident said last year's appropriation did not cover drainage beneath the track and turf, and an added amount would complete the assessment.
The interim manager reviewed the status of each ARPA line, noting which are fully expended and which are lagging, and stated the unallocated amount available.
Delaying implementation to January 1 reduces the first-year cost; later years are an annual subscription, and the finance director's plan to phase in funding was questioned.

budget_items.topic: Final ARPA allocation list by median
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair read the funded items, including a full-amount weekend food kit program, DPW garage floor and roof repairs, and the flat hill detention basin contribution; the total came to roughly $353,500 with a small remainder.
A member noted $125,000 was pulled from the capital plan and several requests, including the school committee's, did not make the list.
The interim manager said unpaid FY24 assessing bills and interim valuation services could be paid from reprogrammed ARPA rather than appropriating new money at fall town meeting.

transfers.description: ARPA consultant for reporting line redirected to ARPA Administration and IT staffing challenges; FY23 tax assessment support line redirected to FY24/FY25 valuation services

decisions.decision: The school committee's Chapter 70 request will be forwarded to the interim town manager for inclusion in the fall town meeting.
The board chose the median tab over the average to rank ARPA requests.
The weekend food kit program will be funded at the full amount.
The sewer commission MUNIS consultant line stays allocated, pending confirmation of whether the finance director's request already covers it.
The interim town manager will work toward a consolidated, non-confidential HR report on staff turnover and exit interview highlights.
Flat hill speed limit decision deferred until the DPW director completes field work.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to redirect two ARPA lines, one to ARPA administration and IT staffing and one to FY24/FY25 valuation services.
The board chose the median tab over the average to rank ARPA requests.
The board voted unanimously to commit the final ARPA allocation list as read by the chair; the weekend food kit program was funded in full.
The school committee's request to appropriate added Chapter 70 money was referred to the interim town manager for the fall town meeting.
Public comment ran long on the vice chair and a possible recall, and a flat hill speed limit decision was deferred until DPW field work is done.

why_it_matters: The ARPA vote fixed which town requests got one-time federal money and which, including the school committee's, did not make the list, so unfunded items may return as asks at town meeting.
Paying overdue assessing and valuation bills from reprogrammed ARPA can mean less new money to appropriate at fall town meeting, where residents vote on any Chapter 70 appropriation to the schools.

The DPW director's field work on flat hill speed limits, after which the board is to take the decision up again.
